properties.description: ISO/SAE 21434 Annex H Table H.2 asset 'Data communication (lamp request)'. Command that switches the headlamp low/high/off (Body control ECU -> power switch actuator, DF-9).

securityGoals.consequence: Front collision with a stationary object during night driving, caused by the headlamp switching off unintentionally (loss of integrity of the lamp request).
securityGoals.formalDescription: The lamp request shall be protected against spoofing and tampering on its way from the body control ECU to the power switch actuator.

securityGoals.consequence: Vehicle cannot be driven at night because the headlamp function was inhibited while parked (loss of availability of the lamp request).
securityGoals.formalDescription: The lamp request shall remain available against flooding of the vehicle bus.
Lamp requests shall be attributable to the sending ECU.

properties.description: ISO/SAE 21434 Annex H Table H.2 asset 'Data communication (oncoming car information)'. Yes/no oncoming-vehicle indication for the automatic high-beam logic (Camera ECU -> power switch actuator, DF-10).

securityGoals.consequence: Drivers of oncoming vehicles are blinded because the headlamp cannot change to low beam (loss of integrity of the oncoming-vehicle information).
securityGoals.formalDescription: The oncoming-car information shall be protected against spoofing and tampering on its way from the Camera ECU to the body control ECU.

securityGoals.consequence: Automatic high beam malfunctions; the headlamp remains at low beam during night driving (loss of availability of the oncoming-vehicle information).
securityGoals.formalDescription: The oncoming-car information shall remain available; its loss shall be detected and lead to low beam.

properties.description: ISO/SAE 21434 Annex H Table H.2 asset 'Headlamp on/off function': switching the headlamps on, off and between low and high beam, from the headlamp switch (SE-1) through the Body control ECU (MP-3) to the power switch actuator (AC-1).

securityGoals.formalDescription: The configuration of the headlamp on/off function shall be protected against disclosure.
The headlamp on/off function shall only act on authentic lamp requests.

securityGoals.consequence: Headlamp function unavailable while parked — operational annoyance, no direct safety effect.
securityGoals.formalDescription: The headlamp on/off function shall remain available against flooding of the vehicle bus.

properties.description: ISO/SAE 21434 Annex H Table H.2 asset 'Firmware of body control ECU'. Firmware image of the body control ECU. NOTE: set dataType to 'firmware' if the StoredDataType vocabulary supports it.

securityGoals.consequence: Disclosure / reverse-engineering of the body control ECU firmware.
Tampering with the body control ECU firmware could alter the lamp-request logic and enable the headlamp-off attack.
securityGoals.formalDescription: The body control ECU shall accept only authentic firmware.

connections.description: Remote update and configuration commands from the mobile network / backend to the Navigation ECU over HTTPS on the cellular link.
connections.name: push remote update [cmd]

properties.notes: Remote update/configuration pushed from the backend to the Navigation ECU over the cellular link. ASSUMPTION flow (cellular counterpart is not defined in Annex H).

connections.description: Media and control commands from the driver's smartphone to the Navigation ECU over Bluetooth.
connections.name: push media control [cmd]

properties.notes: Media/control traffic from the driver's smartphone to the Navigation ECU over Bluetooth. Adjacent-wireless attack surface; link security depends on the pairing mode (worst case Just Works).

connections.description: Diagnostic requests and responses (UDS over CAN) between the OBD-II diagnostic tool and the Gateway ECU.
connections.name: pull diagnostic data [req_resp]

properties.notes: Diagnostic access (UDS-over-CAN) between the OBD-II diagnostic tool and the Gateway ECU. Unauthenticated local access is what enables the OBD-based attack path in Table H.5.

connections.description: Vehicle-state requests from the Navigation ECU to the Gateway ECU and their responses on the internal bus. A compromised Navigation ECU abuses this channel to inject control signals.
connections.name: pull vehicle state [req_resp]

properties.notes: Data communication between the Navigation ECU and the Gateway ECU (Table H.1). Legitimately a vehicle-state request/response; a compromised Navigation ECU abuses this channel to transmit malicious control signals.

connections.description: Cyclic vehicle signals broadcast by the other ECUs on the internal bus and received by the Gateway ECU.
connections.name: stream vehicle signals

properties.notes: Cyclic bus signals broadcast by the Other ECUs onto the internal vehicle bus (assumed CAN). Relevant to the bus-flooding denial-of-service path in Table H.5.

connections.description: Vehicle commands the Gateway ECU forwards to the Body control ECU on the internal bus — the path into the item in the Annex H attack.
connections.name: push vehicle command [cmd]

properties.notes: Control traffic the Gateway ECU forwards to the Body control ECU on the internal bus. This is the path along which the Annex H attack forwards malicious signals into the item.
properties.safetyRationale: Routed control channel from the gateway into the headlamp system; abused in the Annex H spoofing path to inject a false lamp request toward the power switch actuator.

connections.description: Control and configuration commands the Gateway ECU forwards to the Camera ECU on the internal bus.
connections.name: push camera control [cmd]

properties.notes: Control/configuration traffic the Gateway ECU forwards to the Camera ECU on the internal bus.

connections.description: Headlamp mode (low, high, off) from the driver's headlamp switch to the Body control ECU as a hardwired discrete signal.
connections.name: push headlamp mode [cmd]

properties.notes: Driver's headlamp switch position (low/high/off) read by the Body control ECU. Hardwired discrete signal inside the vehicle.

connections.description: The lamp request (low, high, off) from the Body control ECU to the power switch actuator over LIN — asset DA-001 and target of the spoofing and tampering scenarios of Annex H.
connections.name: push lamp request [cmd]

properties.dataTypeNotes: ISO/SAE 21434 Table H.2 asset: 'Data communication (lamp request)'. Cybersecurity properties: Integrity + Availability.
properties.notes: The lamp request (low, high, or off) from the Body control ECU to the power switch actuator. This is the primary asset of the Annex H example and the target of the spoofing/tampering threat scenarios (Table H.4).
properties.safetyRationale: Carries the 'lamp request' that switches the headlamp low/high/off. Loss of integrity can turn the headlamp off during night driving (cannot-drive-at-night / front-collision damage scenarios, Major/Severe impact in Table H.3).

connections.description: Oncoming car status (yes/no) streamed from the Camera ECU to the power switch actuator for automatic high beam — asset DA-003; its denial of service is the second Annex H scenario.
connections.name: stream oncoming car status

properties.dataTypeNotes: ISO/SAE 21434 Table H.2 asset: 'Data communication (oncoming car information)'. Cybersecurity properties: Integrity + Availability.
properties.notes: Oncoming car information (yes or no) streamed from the Camera ECU to the power switch actuator for the automatic high-beam function. Denial of service of this flow is the second Annex H threat scenario.
properties.safetyRationale: Carries the oncoming-car yes/no used by the automatic high-beam logic; denial of service can leave the high beam on and blind oncoming drivers (Moderate impact, Table H.3).

elements.description: Trust boundary of the in-vehicle connectivity domain: the ECUs reachable from outside the vehicle (Navigation ECU, Gateway ECU). Every flow from an external entity into this zone crosses it.
elements.name: Operational environment (in-vehicle connectivity) [OE]

properties.complianceRelevance: ISO/SAE 21434 operational environment (Annex H, Figure H.2 shaded region / Table H.1).
properties.notes: Trust boundary around the operational-environment / in-vehicle connectivity domain. External entities sit outside it; its outer edge (at the cellular, Bluetooth and OBD-II interfaces) is the external-to-vehicle trust transition.
properties.securityAssumptions: In-vehicle connectivity domain (Navigation ECU, Gateway ECU, Other ECUs). Reachable from outside the vehicle via the cellular, Bluetooth and OBD-II interfaces; the Gateway ECU firewall (CAL4, Table H.1) guards the transition into the item.

elements.description: Trust boundary around the externally exposed Navigation ECU (DMZ). The flow from the Navigation ECU to the Gateway ECU leaves it, which makes the gateway the trust transition into the vehicle network.
elements.name: Externally-exposed zone (Navigation ECU) [NECU]

properties.complianceRelevance: ISO/SAE 21434 Annex H — externally reachable ECU / first attack step (Tables H.5/H.6).
properties.notes: Trust boundary isolating the externally-exposed Navigation ECU (DMZ) from the hardened Gateway ECU. The Nav-to-Gateway data flow crosses this boundary, making the gateway firewall an explicit trust transition.
properties.securityAssumptions: Externally-exposed zone containing the Navigation ECU. The ECU terminates the cellular and Bluetooth interfaces and has a firewall to reject invalid external data (Table H.1). First compromise point in the Annex H attack paths.

elements.description: ISO/SAE 21434 item boundary of the analysis: the Camera ECU and the headlamp system. Everything outside it is the operational environment of the item.
elements.name: Item boundary [IB]

properties.notes: ISO/SAE 21434 item boundary — the Camera ECU plus the headlamp system. Not a single physical enclosure but the analysis scope of this TARA; modelled as boundaryType 'custom'. Physically reached only through the vehicle.
properties.safetyRationale: Encloses the headlamp function (lamp-request path); Severe/Major impact scenarios in Table H.3.

elements.description: Headlamp system inside the item boundary: headlamp switch, body control ECU and power switch actuator, installed in the vehicle body.
elements.name: Headlamp system [HS]

properties.notes: Headlamp system sub-boundary nested inside the item boundary: headlamp switch, body control ECU and power switch actuator with the lamps.
properties.safetyRationale: Headlamp system (switch, body control ECU, power switch actuator) controls the headlamp; Severe/Major impact scenarios in Table H.3.

elements.description: Mobile network and OEM backend that reach the Navigation ECU over the cellular interface, e.g. for remote updates. Assumed counterpart; Annex H names none.
elements.name: Mobile network / backend (assumption – not in Annex H)

properties.notes: Mobile network / backend reachable over the cellular interface. ASSUMPTION — no counterpart is named in Annex H for the cellular link; added so the interface has a source and the remote attack path is complete.

threatProfile.rationale: Remote attacker reachable over the cellular link. ISO/SAE 21434 Table H.6 rates 'compromises Navigation ECU from cellular interface' as High attack feasibility (attack-vector-based).

elements.description: The driver's smartphone, paired with the Navigation ECU over Bluetooth for media and control. Annex H Table H.5 starts an attack path from a compromised smartphone.
elements.name: Driver's smartphone

properties.notes: Driver's smartphone, the Bluetooth counterpart of the Navigation ECU. Named in Table H.5, where the attacker compromises it and uses it (with a Bluetooth OBD dongle) as a denial-of-service vector.

threatProfile.rationale: Reachable via Bluetooth pairing to the Navigation ECU. Table H.6 rates the Bluetooth path as Medium feasibility; Table H.5 uses a compromised driver's smartphone as a denial-of-service vector.

elements.description: OBD-II diagnostic tool connected locally to the OBD-II port. It talks UDS to the Gateway ECU; Annex H Table H.5 uses it to send malicious control signals.
elements.name: OBD-II diagnostic tool

properties.notes: OBD-II diagnostic tool with local access to the OBD-II connector. In Table H.5 the attacker sends malicious control signals from the OBD connector, which the Gateway ECU then forwards.

threatProfile.rationale: Requires local physical access to the OBD-II connector. Table H.6 rates the OBD-connector path as Low attack feasibility.

elements.description: Navigation ECU (head unit) in the operational environment. Connected to the outside over cellular and Bluetooth and to the Gateway ECU over the internal bus; the first attack step of the Annex H paths.
elements.name: Navigation ECU

properties.notes: Navigation ECU (head unit) in the operational environment. Externally connected via cellular and Bluetooth; connected to the Gateway ECU by data communication (Table H.1). In every Annex H attack path the attacker first compromises this ECU from the cellular or Bluetooth interface, then transmits malicious control signals toward the gateway.
properties.securitySummary: Internet-facing infotainment/navigation ECU terminating the cellular and Bluetooth interfaces. Firewall on external interfaces per ISO/SAE 21434 Table H.1 assumption. First compromise point in the Annex H attack paths (Tables H.5/H.6).

elements.description: Gateway ECU routing and filtering traffic between the connectivity domain, the OBD-II port and the internal bus of the item. It forwards commands to the Body control ECU and the Camera ECU.
elements.name: Gateway ECU

properties.notes: Gateway ECU routing between the external/connectivity domain and the internal vehicle bus that reaches the item. Strong security controls incl. a firewall function, developed as CAL4 (Table H.1). In the Annex H attack paths it forwards the malicious control signals to the power switch actuator once the Navigation ECU or the OBD-II path is abused.
properties.securitySummary: Central vehicle gateway with firewall, developed as CAL4 per ISO/SAE 21434 Table H.1 assumption. Trust choke point between the connectivity domain (Navigation ECU, OBD-II) and the headlamp item on the internal bus.

elements.description: Camera ECU of the item, outside the headlamp system. It detects oncoming vehicles and streams the oncoming car status to the power switch actuator for automatic high beam.
elements.name: Camera ECU

properties.notes: Camera ECU inside the item boundary but outside the headlamp system sub-boundary. Produces the 'oncoming car information (yes or no)' consumed by the power switch actuator. Denial of service of this information is one of the two Annex H threat scenarios (Table H.4).
properties.securitySummary: In-item smart camera ECU that classifies oncoming vehicles and streams the yes/no result to the power switch actuator for the automatic high-beam function.

elements.description: The driver's headlamp switch (low, high, off). Its position is read by the Body control ECU as a discrete signal.
elements.name: Headlamp switch

properties.notes: Driver's headlamp switch. Sensor/source of the desired headlamp mode (low/high/off) into the body control ECU. Transducer-specific fields left unset — they need the transducer-properties schema.

elements.description: Body control ECU of the headlamp system. It reads the driver's headlamp switch and the gateway commands and sends the lamp request (low, high, off) to the power switch actuator.
elements.name: Body control ECU

properties.internalComponents: Headlamp control logic (low/high/off arbitration), diagnostic services, bus stack.
properties.notes: Body control ECU inside the headlamp system. Receives the driver's switch position and issues the 'lamp request (low, high, or off)' to the power switch actuator. Its firmware is an asset in Table H.2; the lamp request is the asset targeted by the Annex H spoofing/tampering threat scenarios (Table H.4).
properties.safetyRationale: Generates the 'lamp request' that controls the headlamp. Manipulation can unintentionally switch the headlamp off during night driving — rated Severe (S3) / Major impact in ISO/SAE 21434 Table H.3.
properties.securitySummary: Body control ECU inside the headlamp system. Its firmware is a listed asset (Table H.2: Confidentiality + Integrity). Issues the safety-relevant lamp request to the power switch actuator.

elements.description: Power switch actuator that switches the headlamps on, off and between low and high beam, from the lamp request and the oncoming car status.
elements.name: Power switch actuator

properties.notes: Power switch actuator driving the headlamps. Consumes the lamp request from the body control ECU and the oncoming-car status from the camera ECU. Transducer-specific fields left unset — they need the transducer-properties schema.

elements.description: Internal vehicle bus (assumed CAN; Annex H says only 'communication bus') connecting the Gateway ECU, the Camera ECU, the Body control ECU and the other ECUs.
elements.name: CAN

properties.notes: Internal vehicle communication bus. Assumed CAN — Annex H states only 'communication bus' (the CAN detail comes from the separate braking-ECU example in clause 15.6, not from Annex H). Connects the Gateway ECU with the Other ECUs and the item; subject to the bus-flooding DoS path (Table H.5).
properties.safetyRationale: Internal vehicle bus carrying safety-relevant control traffic, including the lamp-request path.

elements.description: The other ECUs on the internal vehicle bus, outside the scope of the item. They broadcast cyclic signals the Gateway ECU routes; a flooding ECU can deny the bus.
elements.name: Other ECUs

properties.notes: Other ECUs sharing the internal vehicle bus. Modelled as an External Entity because they are out of the analysis scope for the headlamp item and appear in no Annex H attack path. Kept as a black box; the bus-flooding DoS possibility is carried on the CAN data flow.

threatProfile.rationale: Other in-vehicle ECUs on the shared bus, out of analysis scope for this item. A compromised bus participant could flood the communication bus (Table H.5 DoS path); that residual threat is tracked on the bus data flow, not on this out-of-scope node.

elements.description: OBD-II diagnostic connector (SAE J1962) routed to the Gateway ECU, carrying UDS over CAN. Local physical attack surface.
elements.name: OBD-II

properties.notes: OBD-II diagnostic connector (SAE J1962) routed to the Gateway ECU; UDS-over-CAN. Local-physical attack surface (Table H.6 Low feasibility).

info.description: ISO/SAE 21434 TARA example — automotive headlamp system (based on the worked example in Annex H). Exercises the iso-21434 preset: SFOP damage-scenario impact, per-element STRIDE (per-interaction disabled), attack-tree attack-potential feasibility, and R = I x L.
info.name: Headlamp System (ISO/SAE 21434)

assumptions.text: The internal vehicle bus is CAN without message authentication; Annex H names only a communication bus.
The Navigation ECU is reachable from the mobile network / OEM backend; this path is an addition to Annex H.
Changing the body control ECU firmware needs the ECU opened on the bench and specialised equipment; the debug interface is locked in series production.
The Gateway ECU filters traffic between the connectivity domain and the vehicle bus and is the only path from the Navigation ECU and the OBD-II port to the headlamp system.

functions.description: Switches the headlamp on and off and between low and high beam on the driver's request.
functions.name: Headlamp on / off

functions.description: Changes to low beam when the Camera ECU detects an oncoming vehicle.
functions.name: Automatic high beam

functions.description: Workshop update of the body control ECU firmware over the OBD-II port.
functions.name: Firmware update of the body control ECU

architecture.text: The body control ECU reads the headlamp switch and the oncoming-car status from the Camera ECU and sends the lamp request to the power switch actuator. See the DFD: flows DF-6, DF-9 and DF-10 inside the item; the Gateway ECU routes vehicle commands from the connectivity domain.

boundary.text: The item comprises the headlamp system (headlamp switch, body control ECU, power switch actuator) and the Camera ECU that detects oncoming vehicles. Navigation ECU, Gateway ECU, OBD-II port and the other ECUs on the vehicle bus belong to the operational environment; the item exchanges data with them over the vehicle bus only.

constraints.text: Teaching example: the Annex H data are completed by assumptions ASM-01 … ASM-04. Safety-relevant consequences (blinding, front collision) are rated as cybersecurity damage scenarios; the safety analysis itself is out of scope.

environment.text: Passenger car in road traffic, day and night driving and parking. External interfaces of the vehicle reach the item indirectly: cellular and Bluetooth through the Navigation ECU, local diagnosis through the OBD-II port. Workshops have physical access during maintenance.
